payload.title: Fix #1748: make cloud-metadata/private-range denylist non-overridable

payload.author: S0412-2007
payload.body:
@utksh1 ready for review.

One thing worth calling out: the original issue's exact repro (default denylist missing 169.254.169.254 entirely) doesn't reproduce on current `main` — that part looks like it was already fixed at some point. What I found instead is a related, still-live version of the same bug: `settings.network_denylist` is a single Pydantic field, and setting `SECUSCAN_NETWORK_DENYLIST` via env var *replaces* rather than merges with its default. So an operator who customizes the denylist at all silently loses the metadata/private-range protection, even though the code comment claims it's "always enforced."

This PR splits those ranges into a `MANDATORY_DENYLIST` constant that's not read from config at all, so they can't be dropped via env var — `network_denylist` is now purely additive. Added a regression test (`test_operator_denylist_override_does_not_drop_mandatory_ranges`) that reproduces this scenario directly.

Happy to adjust the approach if you'd rather keep denylist config fully in Settings and handle the merge differently (e.g. a validator that appends instead of replaces) — went with the module-constant approach since it guarantees the protection can't be disabled even by a misconfigured env var, not just a careless one.

payload.body: The current upsert logic (`SELECT` followed by `INSERT` or `UPDATE`) in `_persist_finding` introduces a race condition. If two tasks concurrently try to persist the same finding, both will see no existing row, and the second one to `INSERT` will fail with a `UNIQUE constraint failed` exception on `(owner_id, finding_group_id)`. Please use SQLite's native `INSERT INTO ... ON CONFLICT (owner_id, finding_group_id) DO UPDATE SET ...` to make the upsert atomic.

payload.author: utksh1

payload.body: The in-memory fallback implementation introduces a memory leak. Because `bucket_min` and `bucket_hr` include the timestamp window in the key (e.g., `f"{ip}:minute:{minute_window}"`), new keys are created every minute and hour for every active IP. The cleanup loop truncates the timestamps but never deletes empty keys from `_fallback_history`. Please add `if not self._fallback_history[key]: del self._fallback_history[key]` after filtering stale entries to prevent unbounded memory growth.

payload.author: utksh1

Thanks for the PR! The in-memory fallback implementation looks solid and cleanly mirrors the sliding window algorithm.

1. When Redis fails (e.g. mocking a connection error), the fallback circuit breaker engages and HTTP 429s are still properly enforced using the in-memory dictionary.
2. When Redis recovers, the circuit breaker disengages and returns to normal operation.

Once tests are added, we can get this merged!

Closing as invalid because:
- They are duplicates of each other (only one could ever merge; the rest would immediately conflict).
